children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

=== YOUR SITUATION PROFILE ===
You live in the UK.
You are asking about Child Benefit for 1 child:
  - Alex is 18 years old and lives with you.

Here are the exact details of your circumstances to use when answering the agent's questions:

Regarding Alex:
  - Claimant lives in the UK
  - Child is 18 and in approved education
  - Child lives with claimant
  - Child is not in local authority care
  - Child is not in hospital or residential accommodation
  - Child is not fostered
  - Child does not work 24+ hours/week
  - Child has not started an apprenticeship in England
  - Child does not receive qualifying benefits in their own right

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start the assessment process.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To start, I need to know about your child. **How old is your child?**

This matters because:
- Children **under 16** may automatically qualify
- Children **aged 16-19** may qualify if they're in approved education or training
- Children **aged 20 or over** generally don't qualify

Please tell me your child's age.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Hello! Thanks for helping me with this.

I have one child - Alex, who's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! 

So Alex is 18 years old, which means they fall into the 16-19 age category. For children in this age group, eligibility depends on whether they're in approved education or training.

Let me check the next step for this situation.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I need to understand Alex's current education or training situation.

**Is Alex currently:**
1. **In approved education or training** (such as school, college, or an approved training course), OR
2. **Recently left education or training** (within the last few months), OR
3. **Neither** - not in education/training and didn't recently leave

Which of these applies to Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex is currently in education - they're studying for their A-levels at college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Since Alex is studying for their A-levels at college, they are currently in education. Let me check the education requirements.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! A-levels are an approved (non-advanced) qualification for Child Benefit purposes. Now I need to check a few more details about Alex's education:

**1. Is Alex's course full-time?** (This means at least 12 hours per week of supervised study - not including homework or private study)

**2. Is the course funded by an employer, or does Alex have an agreed future job with an employer who is funding the course?**

**3. Is Alex married or in a civil partnership?** (This only affects eligibility if they're not financially dependent on you)

Please let me know the answers to these questions.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Yes, it's a full-time course - they're at college most weekdays with all their classes and supervised study time.

No, it's not funded by an employer, and there's no job agreement involved. It's just regular college.

And no, Alex isn't married or in a civil partnership.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Alex's situation meets all the education requirements:
- ✓ A-levels are an approved qualification
- ✓ Full-time course (12+ hours per week of supervised study)
- ✓ Not employer-funded
- ✓ Not married/in civil partnership

Let me move to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's work situation:

**Does Alex work less than 24 hours per week (or is not in paid work at all)?**

It's okay if Alex has a part-time job alongside their studies, as long as it's under 24 hours per week.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work at all. They're just focused on their studies at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Alex is not working, which means they meet this requirement. Let me continue with the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about benefits:

**Is Alex receiving any benefits in their own right?** Specifically, I'm asking about:
- Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Universal Credit
- Or similar benefits claimed in their own name

Is Alex **NOT** receiving any of these benefits? (In other words, is Alex free from claiming these benefits?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: That's right - Alex isn't receiving any benefits in their own name. No Universal Credit, ESA, or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about apprenticeships:

**Is Alex doing an apprenticeship?**

This is important because most apprenticeships disqualify someone from Child Benefit (except Foundation Apprenticeships in Wales, which are approved). 

Since you mentioned Alex is doing A-levels at college, I'm assuming they're not in an apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't doing an apprenticeship. Like I said, they're just doing A-levels at college - regular sixth form studies.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Alex is not in an apprenticeship, so that's fine. Now let me move on to check your eligibility as the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check your residency status as the claimant. 

**Do you normally live in the UK?**

If yes, that's the simplest path to meet the residency requirement. If not, there are other special circumstances that might apply (such as having settled or pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or being a Crown servant abroad).

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - I'm based in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! You meet the residency requirement by normally living in the UK. Now let me check the next requirement.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check if you're responsible for Alex. You can meet this requirement in different ways:

**Which of the following applies to you?**

1. **You live with Alex**, OR
2. **You contribute to Alex's upkeep** (paying at least the equivalent of Child Benefit towards their care - things like food, clothes, pocket money, housing costs), OR
3. **You pay maintenance** under a court order or agreement

Which of these applies to your situation with Alex?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! You meet the responsibility requirement by living with Alex. Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check about other potential claimants:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

For example:
- Alex's other parent
- Another family member or guardian
- Anyone else

If yes, are you and that person in agreement about transferring the claim to you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! Let me continue to the next check.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Now I need to check Alex's living situation:

**Which of these best describes where Alex is currently living?**

1. **In hospital** (as an in-patient)
2. **In local authority care** (looked after by the council)
3. **Fostered** (living with foster carers)
4. **Normal living** (at home with you, as you mentioned)

Based on what you've told me, it sounds like Alex is living normally at home with you. Is that correct?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex is just living at home with me normally. They're not in hospital, care, or fostered or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Let me continue with the assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
One final question:

**Is the local council paying towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance?**

In other words, is the council providing any financial support for Alex's living costs or care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council isn't paying anything towards Alex's accommodation or maintenance. We're just a regular family - I support Alex myself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Excellent! Let me check the final outcome.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## 🎉 Great News - You Are Eligible for Child Benefit!

Based on the information you've provided, **you meet all the eligibility requirements** for Child Benefit for Alex.

### Why You're Eligible:

✓ **Alex qualifies as a child** - At 18 years old, Alex is in the 16-19 age group and studying full-time A-levels (an approved, non-advanced qualification)  
✓ **Education requirements met** - Full-time course with 12+ hours per week of supervised study  
✓ **Not working full-time** - Alex is not working at all  
✓ **No disqualifying benefits** - Alex is not receiving Universal Credit or ESA  
✓ **Not in a disqualifying apprenticeship** - Regular college studies  
✓ **You meet residency requirements** - You normally live in the UK (Manchester)  
✓ **You're responsible for Alex** - Alex lives at home with you  
✓ **No competing claims** - No one else is claiming for Alex  
✓ **Normal living situation** - Alex lives at home normally  
✓ **No council support** - The council is not paying towards Alex's care  

### Next Steps to Claim:

1. **Apply online or by post** using form CH2
2. **Provide proof of identity** for yourself and Alex
3. **Provide Alex's birth certificate** or adoption certificate
4. **Be aware of the High Income Child Benefit Charge** - If you or your partner earn over £60,000, you may need to pay back some or all of the benefit through your tax return
5. **Payments** are made every 4 weeks (or weekly if you're a single parent or receiving certain benefits)

For more information and to apply, visit: https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit/how-to-claim

Do you have any questions about applying or about the Child Benefit?
